newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Telecom says call back distorts flows.
newsitem.headline: HK Telecom says call back distorts flows.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd said on Wednesday the rapid growth of call back services was distorting world telecom traffic flows and hampering the company's network development and investment planning.
"It is distorting the way in which we plan our networks," Keith Harrison, Hongkong Telecom's director of international, told reporters.
With a call back service, a Hong Kong-to-U.S. call is automatically bounced back as a U.S.-to-Hong Kong call and charged at U.S. rates.
Through another system called refile, a Hong Kong-to-third country call turns into two U.S. origin calls.

As call back and refile grows, the United States is turning into a telecom hub, and Hongkong Telecom's two-way traffic with the United States is growing 50 percent a year even though overall traffic is only growing 10 percent a year.
That means rising demand for trans-Pacific capacity even though many of the calls may actually be between Hong Kong and Europe, South America or elsewhere in Asia.

"There has been a dramatic shift in traffic growth rates in the last couple of years, which has put up a significant demand for capacity across the Pacific and a commensurate slacking off of demand to some other places," Harrison said.

"So we are having now to reconsider a lot of our plans for submarine cable systems to make sure we are able to provide, to an acceptable quality level, capacity between here and wherever the call has to go via wherever," he said.

Submarine cables have a lifespan of 20 years and Hongkong Telecom could be looking at investing tens of millions of U.S. dollars in them in the next five years, so rapidly changing traffic patterns was a major problem for planning, he said.
